person: Reggie Banks is 61 and works three days a week as the finance person for a small snack brand that sells through two national distributors. He is a retired grocery accounts-payable man who lives in spreadsheets, and he reads at 175% zoom because of macular degeneration. The founder has handed him the trademark docket of twelve registrations because nobody else tracks it, and it lives in an old spreadsheet. He wants each filing explained line by line, with every fee and date shown so he can add them up himself, and he will not let anything be declared under oath that he has not seen proven.
stated_up_front: I need to go through our twelve trademark registrations and see which ones need a maintenance filing right now, and file only those. Please go slowly and show me each one with its dates and fees in plain lines, because I read at big zoom.

facts.about: the brand and what is on the docket
facts.truth: Brightfield Snacks sells granola bars, trail mix, rice crisps and snack seasonings; twelve registrations sit on the docket, kept in an old spreadsheet and now in the Markwick desk.

facts.about: the two Section 8 filings that are due now with real photos
facts.truth: The BRIGHTFIELD word mark in class 29 (trail mix) and the BRIGHTFIELD logo in class 30 (granola bars) are both in their sixth-year window; each has a real shelf photo from the Shopify product pages.

facts.about: the renewal that deletes discontinued goods
facts.truth: The OAT & ORCHARD registration is at its ten-year renewal; the apple-cinnamon rice crisps were discontinued in March 2023 and must be deleted, while the granola clusters are still sold.

facts.about: the renewal in its grace period
facts.truth: The CRUNCHWELL registration missed its ten-year date; it is in the grace period with five days left as of 9 October 2026, and needs both the late surcharge and the renewal fees.

facts.about: the Section 8 in its grace period
facts.truth: The TRAILSIDE TREATS registration missed its sixth-year date and is in its grace period; it is still sold as trail mix bars and a photo exists.
SNAPPEA SPARK was registered in 2023, so its window has not opened; Reggie keeps it on the sheet with a note to look in 2028.
The HARVEST HOLLOW Section 8 was filed in the spring and the USPTO acceptance notice is in the Outlook mail.
The PEPPERMILL POP mark was assigned in 2024 to a popcorn company, and its new owner's mail still arrives at Brightfield.
The old MUNCHBARN registration passed its grace period in 2025 and was cancelled; the brand stopped using it.

facts.about: goods never sold and the ended line
facts.truth: Registration covering chia pudding cups lists goods the brand only mocked up and never sold; a SNOWCAP rice cake line ended in 2025 and is not to be declared.

facts.about: who does the filing and who decides
facts.truth: Reggie prepares the docket; the founder, Dana Whitcomb, has to sign off on anything filed under oath.

unknowns: the exact dollar fee per class and the grace-period surcharge amount
what makes a photo count as an acceptable specimen rather than a mock-up
the exact deadline and window rule for each registration type
whether deleting discontinued goods costs anything extra
